According to information received by the Hana Human Rights Organization, Sirvan Shabani, 25, an artist and musician who leads a pop and traditional orchestra, along with Khosrow Mohammadinia and Masoud Tushmalani, are currently being held in Qezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. Hana has reported that these three individuals were arrested on 19 Dey 1404 by security forces, at the same time as protests in Islamshahr, and were subsequently held in solitary confinement for a period. According to this report, after months of being held in solitary confinement and what Hana has described as "obtaining forced confessions," they have been transferred to Qezel Hesar Prison. @VahidHeadline 📡 @VahidOnline

entry.summary:

Farzaneh Fasihi, Iran's Olympic runner, responded to recent remarks by Ehsan Haddadi, head of the Athletics Federation of the Islamic Republic, calling him the "most notorious athlete in Iran's history" and writing that young athletes should treat him as a "cautionary tale," not a role model. In a text published on her Instagram page, Farzaneh Fasihi addressed Ehsan Haddadi, writing: "In your parallel world, you should have been behind bars and enjoyed no civil rights whatsoever, but what can we do — here they've handed the fate of hundreds and thousands of pure and innocent young people over to you, and now you've taken to lecturing." This reaction came after Ehsan Haddadi said in an interview with the state website "Varzesh 3" on Wednesday, 8 Mehr 1405, regarding female athletes: "I hold meetings with female runners and tell them you can become an influencer like many female athletes with 30,000, 50,000, 300,000 followers, or you can become a champion." Farzaneh Fasihi also wrote, referring to Reyhaneh Mobini, Zahra Zarei, and Fatemeh Mohiti-Zadeh, among Iran's female track and field athletes, that the thought of them wanting to follow Ehsan Haddadi's teachings is "like a nightmare" to her. She further addressed the head of the Athletics Federation, writing: "Being honorable has nothing to do with medals and championships. You have proven that even with a saddlebag full of medals, one can still go backward and become despised by a nation." Farzaneh Fasihi's reference to "behind bars" goes back to Ehsan Haddadi's judicial case in the 1390s. In that case, accusations of sexual assault and rape were brought against Ehsan Haddadi, and the court ruled for imprisonment, flogging, and a fine. However, the case was closed with the intervention of security institutions. In recent years, some prominent Iranian female track and field athletes have also left the country. Elnaz Kompani, Iran's record holder in the 60-meter hurdles, announced her emigration to America, and before her, Maryam Tousi, Iran's women's indoor 200-meter record holder, had emigrated to America.@VahidHeadline📡 @VahidOnline
